language.script: Khmer script — a Brahmic-derived abugida, the longest alphabet in the world, with tall, ornate vertical strokes

terrainDescription.zh: 洞里薩湖與湄公河氾濫平原是主要農業精華區，西南部豆蔻山脈仍保有大片雨林，另有一小段泰國灣海岸線。
terrainDescription.en: The Tonlé Sap lake and Mekong floodplain dominate the agricultural heartland; the Cardamom Mountains in the southwest hold significant rainforest cover, with a short stretch of Gulf of Thailand coastline.

plate.color: white background, black text, Latin letters + digits with province name in Khmer (top) and English (bottom)

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Stone bollards, most often red-and-white striped, or red top with white base and a reflector set into the red band

utilityPole.transformerMount: Two common types: a square "ladder-style" pole with indents not reaching the top or bottom, or a round pole with small holes — distinguishable from Thailand's square poles, whose pinholes run the full length

historicalContext.zh: 高棉文字約一千多年前由南印度婆羅米系字母演變而來，書寫時單詞間不留空格，垂直筆畫高聳，雖與泰文、寮文同源，但視覺上仍可明顯區分。
historicalContext.en: Khmer script, adapted from a southern Indian Brahmi-derived alphabet over a thousand years ago, has no spaces between words and tall vertical strokes that make it visually distinct from neighboring Thai and Lao scripts despite sharing the same ultimate ancestor.
